chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:

Regarding a female slave who has entered into a contract of manumission (mukattabah) and her master has sexual intercourse with her, causing her to become pregnant: he must pay her the dowry of her equal (in status/value), and she is granted more time to pay off her remaining debt. If she cannot pay, she becomes an 'Umm al-Walad' (mother of a child who secures her manumission upon her master's death). This does not contradict the first hadith, because in that hadith it is not stated that he is not subject to any punishment (hadd), and the first hadith is detailed, so it is more appropriate to follow it.

key_terms.أُمَّاتِ الْأَوْلَادِ: Mother of a child (a slave who gives birth to her master's child)
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَةٍ: Contract of manumission where a slave pays a fixed sum for freedom
key_terms.يَطَؤُهَا: He has sexual intercourse with her

ai.seo_question: What are the financial and legal consequences for a master who impregnates his female slave who is paying for her own manumission?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi presents this ruling in *al-Istibsar* to resolve apparent contradictions between hadiths regarding the punishment (*hadd*) for a master having intercourse with his *mukattabah* slave, clarifying that the absence of *hadd* does not negate financial compensation. The text establishes a tiered legal consequence: the master must pay the dowry of her equal (*mahr al-mithl*) and grant an extension for her debt, with the ultimate outcome being her emancipation as an *Umm al-Walad* if she defaults. This highlights the Shia juristic principle of prioritizing specific details (*mufassal*) over general statements to determine the final legal status.
